summary: 7-year-old girl with known peanut allergy, 15 minutes after a biscuit at a party: stridor, wheeze, facial swelling, urticaria, vomiting; HR 150, RR 36, SpO₂ 92 %, BP 88/50, 24 kg. RCUK 2021: IM adrenaline 300 micrograms (6-12 years).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Swollen face and noisy breathing after eating
inputs.hpi: Here with her father for review after an umbilical hernia repair. Ate a biscuit at a party 15 minutes ago; it contained peanut. Known peanut allergy, auto-injector left at home. Now swollen face, rash, vomited twice, noisy breathing.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Anaphylaxis (peanut) in a child
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Food anaphylaxis with stridor, wheeze and hypotension in a 7-year-old: IM adrenaline 300 micrograms now, 999, repeat after 5 minutes if no improvement.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Acute Cholecystitis | 2. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis | 3. Peptic Ulcer Disease. PANE has no anaphylaxis node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add an anaphylaxis rule/prompt (acute urticaria/angioedema + airway, breathing or circulation compromise, especially after a drug or food) -> emergency with "IM adrenaline (1 mg/mL): 500 micrograms adult / 300 micrograms 6-12 y / 150 micrograms <6 y, repeat after 5 min; call 999; lie flat; oxygen; IV fluid"; and a PANE/triage node so it can appear in the differential.

guideline.name: Resuscitation Council UK - Emergency treatment of anaphylaxis: guidelines for healthcare providers
guideline.section: IM adrenaline (1 mg/mL) is the first-line treatment: adult and child >12 years 500 micrograms, child 6-12 years 300 micrograms, 6 months-6 years 150 micrograms; repeat after 5 minutes if no improvement; refractory anaphylaxis (no improvement after two IM doses) -> adrenaline infusion with critical care; antihistamines are not first-line and corticosteroids are no longer advised routinely; IV fluid bolus for shock
guideline.citation: Resuscitation Council UK. Emergency treatment of anaphylaxis: guidelines for healthcare providers. London: RCUK; May 2021.

rationale: Paediatric permutation: the adrenaline dose is age-banded (RCUK 2021: 300 micrograms at 6-12 years), and adult shock thresholds do not apply.
